solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wintry weather in south at present

parts.note: at present means now, at this moment

explanation.surface: A weather report: it's wintry in the south right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling flakes of frozen water are the classic example of wintry weather.

clue.text: Initially, neither of us is hard to feed

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word neither

parts.note: of us is the possessive our
taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Neither of us finds it hard to feed someone, at least at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to provide food and sustenance, a synonym of the verb feed.

clue.text: Joker aboard truck

parts.note: a wag is a joker, a witty person
aboard means on, as on a ship or train

explanation.surface: A prankster is riding on a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a goods vehicle, so a synonym for a truck, especially a railway one.

clue.text: View of country importing gold

indicators.note: importing means bringing something in, so one piece goes inside the country

parts.note: Panama is a Central American country
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An opinion about a nation that imports bullion.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, sweeping view of a landscape, a synonym for a view.

clue.text: Comrade, drink up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A toast to a fellow comrade: drink up!
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is a friend or mate, a synonym of comrade.

clue.text: Very recently made top state

parts.note: something very recently made is new
a jersey is a knitted top, a jumper

explanation.surface: A brand-new top in excellent condition.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty states of the USA, an example of a state.

clue.text: Extremist spoke about start of communism

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the spoke wraps round the letter

parts.note: a radial is a spoke, a line running out from a centre

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the word communism

explanation.surface: A political firebrand spoke on how communism began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like a verb of speech but is the noun: a wheel's spoke is a RADIAL, which goes about C.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical holds extreme views seeking root-and-branch change, so is an extremist.

clue.text: Medical Officer on vessel gets to wear black, perhaps

parts.note: an urn is a vessel, a large vase or container

explanation.surface: A military doctor aboard ship has to dress in black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but here it is a container; 'on' merely joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing black is one traditional way to grieve, so it illustrates grieving by example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Dwelling of a French girl in Cockney area

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the London district

parts.note: Bow is an East London district; true Cockneys are born within sound of Bow Bells
un is French for a
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: The home of a French girl living in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: BOW is a district in East London, the traditional heart of Cockney country.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a single-storey house, a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Beginning to describe strange percussion instrument

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word describe

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: Starting to describe an unusual instrument from the percussion section.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum is struck to make sound, the most familiar example of a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Wrong about grand gesture

indicators.note: about means going round, so the wrong wraps round the letter

parts.note: a sin is a wrong, a moral offence
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone is mistaken about a grand gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a gesture made with the hands to convey meaning, so a synonym.

clue.text: Islamic symbol in curved street

definitions.meaning: the moon-shaped emblem associated with Islam
a road built in an arc, common in British street names

explanation.surface: An Islamic emblem found on a curving road.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the shape of the moon's thin sliver: the Islamic emblem and an arc-shaped British street.

clue.text: Escape quickly after seeing copper close to flat with ladder

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: close to picks the final letter of the word flat

parts.note: and means with, together with
a run is a ladder in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: A burglar flees a flat on seeing a policeman, carrying a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the element; 'ladder' is the snag in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut and run is an idiom for making a hasty getaway, fleeing rather than staying.

clue.text: Fellow cut rent for ski lodge

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a fellow
to let is to rent out a property

explanation.surface: A man reduces the rent on a ski lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of CHAP, giving CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden Alpine house, typically used for ski holidays.

clue.text: Members cheek fielder

parts.note: legs are limbs, members of the body
lip means cheek, insolent talk

explanation.surface: Club members insult a cricket fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG SLIP is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the player standing at that close catching position is called by its name, so a fielder.

clue.text: I'm sadly having to go back for a highly seasoned sausage

indicators.note: to go back means the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written, I and M
alas is an exclamation meaning sadly

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having to return a spicy sausage to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' looks like an anagram signal but means ALAS; IM + ALAS read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a strongly spiced cured Italian sausage, so it fits the description.

clue.text: A blemish covered by mother's cosmetic

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped around, so these letters sit inside the mother

parts.note: ma is mother; the 's stands for is, a link
a scar is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Mum uses her make-up to hide a mark on her skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on 'mother' stands for 'is', a link, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is make-up applied to darken eyelashes, an example of a cosmetic.

clue.text: Food sent back, and, for Fritz, last of barley wine

indicators.note: sent back means the word is reversed

parts.note: grub is informal for food
und is German for and; Fritz stands for a German

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word barley

explanation.surface: A German diner returns his meal and finishes his barley wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barley wine' tempts as a phrase, but only 'wine' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgundy is the wine from the French region of that name, red or white.

clue.text: Join squad, English

parts.note: a unit is a squad, a group of soldiers or police

explanation.surface: An instruction to enlist in an English team.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring things together, a synonym for the verb join.

clue.text: Thin fog may be avoided, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: something that may be avoided can be missed

explanation.surface: A light fog might be steered clear of, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a light haze of water droplets, a thinner form of fog.

clue.text: Saw bishop out of bed, having risen

indicators.note: in a down clue, risen means the word is read upwards, backwards
out of means the bishop is removed

parts.note: a bottom is a bed, as of a river or sea
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop was seen getting out of bed after rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not the past of see but a saying. Removing B from BOTTOM leaves OTTOM, which reads MOTTO upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, and a motto is a short maxim, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Help retired head of lyceum to make call

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: aid is help

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word lyceum

explanation.surface: Assistance for a school's retired headmaster to make a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: To dial is to tap in a number on a telephone, i.e. place a phone call.

clue.text: Target of ridicule in genuine denial

indicators.note: in means this piece goes inside the word for genuine

parts.note: real means genuine
a butt is the target of jokes or ridicule

explanation.surface: A laughing stock genuinely denies everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a refutation of a charge or claim, a form of denial.

clue.text: Extra purchase, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to buy is to purchase

explanation.surface: Word has it that something extra was bought.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched, counted among the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket extra is a run not credited to a batsman, and byes are one kind.

clue.text: Displaced persons, finally, receive an answer

indicators.note: displaced means moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the word receive

explanation.surface: Refugees at last get a reply to their request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Displaced persons' looks like a fixed phrase for refugees, but 'Displaced' rearranges PERSONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply, a synonym for an answer.

clue.text: Fine Hungarian wine needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet wine from Hungary

explanation.surface: A well-known Hungarian wine that needs no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is an informal word for all right or acceptable, a synonym of fine.
